entries.title: Watch astronaut Christina Koch and Google’s James Manyika discuss space, technology, and discovery.
entries.summary: Christina Koch sits down with James Manyika, Google’s Senior Vice President of Research, Labs, Technology & Society.
entries.content:
In the latest episode of our Dialogues on Technology and Society series, NASA astronaut, engineer, and scientist Christina Koch sits down with James Manyika, Google’s Senior Vice President of Research, Labs, Technology & Society.

Christina reflects on her trailblazing career — from spending 328 days aboard the International Space Station and conducting the historic first all-female spacewalk, to journeying around the Moon on NASA’s Artemis II mission.

She and James discuss viewing Earth as an electric blue “lifeboat” from 250,000 miles away, and the vital partnership between astronauts, robotics, and AI. Christina also explores the big question—“Are we alone?”—and shares her advice for future explorers: do what scares you, and support the people around you.

Watch the full dialogue to hear more.

entries.title: DevFest is back
entries.summary: Animation of the text "{DevFest} 2026 Join us! Google Developer Groups" with a globe icon, asterisk icon, icon
entries.content:
DevFest season is officially back. From October 1 through December 31, 2026, nearly a million developers and builders will gather for the world’s largest community-led technology conference.

Hosted around the world by Google Developer Groups (GDGs), DevFest helps everyone — from seasoned software engineers to emerging solution builders — gain practical, hands-on experience with Google’s AI technologies.

What to expect at DevFest 2026

Under this year’s theme: "Build, Secure, Scale: Developers and Builders in the Agentic Era," the 2026 season prioritizes hands-on experimentation at every event. Attendees will engage directly with tools across Google’s stack — including Gemini, Google AI Studio, Google Antigravity, Google Cloud, Firebase, Android, Flutter, Angular, and Web MCP — through live codelabs, workshops, and agent-athons.

The tracks this year reflect three core realities for modern software development:

  • It’s never been easier to build. New tools allow more people and teams to prototype and deploy faster than ever.
  • What you build should be safe and secure. Speed cannot come at the expense of stability. Building in the agentic era requires rigorous focus on secure deployment, data privacy, and responsible AI guardrails.
  • You can work with production-ready infrastructure. Google provides top-of-class models to help builders and developers scale reliably from day one.

How to connect with local communities, globally

DevFest is built by the community, for the community. While backed by Google, each GDG curates its agenda and tailors each event to serve the specific needs and challenges of its local tech ecosystem. GDGs design their DevFests to foster an inclusive, welcoming environment where participants collaborate and uplevel their skills together.

Get involved

With more than 800 events planned across 115 countries, DevFest offers a space to sharpen your skills, test new architectures, and connect with the community.

You can find Your Local Event by visiting the DevFest Event Directory and keep up with the conversation by using #DevFest across social channels.

entries.title: We’re exploring a potential data center in Lea County, New Mexico.
entries.summary: Google is exploring a new data center project in Lea County, New Mexico. While discussions are ongoing, we recognize residents are asking questions about data center dev…
entries.content:
Google is exploring a new data center project in Lea County, New Mexico. While discussions are ongoing, we recognize residents are asking questions about data center development, so we want to be transparent and start our conversation with the community early.

Our goal in Lea County is simple: serve as long-term partners who can be counted on to do the right thing in support of the places we call home. That includes responsibly managing vital water resources, paying for 100% of the energy we use and infrastructure we need, and showing up as active members of the community.

Though many details remain outstanding, we’re excited about the possibilities that exist in Lea County, and look forward to sharing more as the project progresses.

entries.title: Three Google supported projects premiere during the 83rd Venice International Film Festival.
entries.summary: Google shares details on three projects that use technology to push the boundaries of human creativity that premiered during the 83rd Venice Film Festival.
entries.content:
During this year’s Venice International Film Festival, Google’s 100 ZEROS team — which partners with filmmakers to explore emerging tech — supported three groundbreaking Extended Reality (XR) projects. They’re all meant to be experienced on Android XR and leverage tools like conversational AI powered by Gemini and Vertex AI, spatial film and 3D stereoscopic depth to expand the canvas of storytelling while keeping human creativity at the center.

Discover the lineup:

  • NEVATARS: A mixed-reality animated short by Andy Serkis filled with Gemini-powered conversations and interactive moments that tell a story about embracing your creative voice.
  • Galápagos: The Last Eden: An immersive XR journey narrated by Margot Robbie that brings nature to life and invites viewers to interact with a Gemini powered, digital Charles Darwin.
  • Sedona: A psychological thriller teaser by Asylm Studios that uses Google’s 2D-to-3D XR auto-spatialization technology to dive straight into suspense on YouTube.

To learn more, head over to the Google Italy blog.

entries.title: Dreambeans: Daily stories, brewed just for you, now available to all accounts in the U.S.
entries.summary: In June, Google Labs introduced Dreambeans, an experiment that creates personalized daily collections of stories. Now, Dreambeans is available to all accounts in the U.S…
entries.content:
In June, Google Labs introduced Dreambeans, an experiment that creates personalized daily collections of stories. Now, Dreambeans is available to all accounts 1 in the U.S. (18+) on Android and iOS.

Every dreambean is a combination of:

  • Personalized topics: This could be everything from places to explore, shows to watch, or a reminder of upcoming events.
  • Connected apps: Distilled information from the Google apps you select, including Calendar, Gmail, Photos, Search, YouTube, and now Gemini.

If you’ve connected Google Photos, Dreambeans can incorporate visuals of you and your loved ones into your stories and provide thoughtful ways you can engage with them.

Discovered something you like? Dive deeper into any story to learn more, bookmark for later, or easily share with others to spark inspiration.

Share your feedback to make your stories even better over time. Download Dreambeans and start dreaming today.

entries.title: 3 ways to prep for your next big race with Search
entries.summary: Illustration on a blue background of technicolor runners with a magnifying glass and Gemini spark overlaid
entries.content:
As people look for ways to unplug and touch grass, running-related searches are spiking: Searches like “run club,” “how to choose running shoes,” and “how to train for a marathon” have reached all-time highs this year.

Running a race requires grit, strength, and (a surprising amount of) organization. Fortunately, Search’s AI features make it easier than ever to get your race plan together. Here are three ways Search can help you make it across the finish line.

1. Create a training plan that’s specific to you and your neighborhood.

Whether you’re a beginner or a seasoned runner with over a dozen races under your belt, having the right training plan is key to finishing the race. AI Mode in Search can help you map out your strategy and develop a detailed plan. Select the Canvas tool from the plus (+) menu and ask it to build a schedule for you, recommending cross-training and strength-building strategies. You can also discover fresh perspectives from sites and creators across the web. Try asking, “Help me make a sub 4.5hr training plan for the Texas Marathon with different routes I can run around Montrose. I'm currently running 4x a week with my longest run typically being 7-9 miles.”

2. Fuel your run with custom playlists.

Now that you’ve selected your race and have a plan in place, it’s time to hit the road. As many runners are well aware, when it comes to race training — especially for longer distances — mental endurance is as important as physical endurance. Finding ways to cope with the boredom and stay energized during a long run is crucial. If you choose to connect your YouTube Music account with Search, you can ask AI Mode to help create a custom playlist for your run so you can stay motivated and listen to your favorite artists on the go.

3. Discover the right gear to keep moving.

Sometimes going the distance comes down to having the right shoes and running gear, but it can be difficult to narrow down your choices. Search can make race-prep shopping a lot easier, allowing you to search for products that address your constraints — like road shoes for wide feet, lightweight hydration vests under $80, or anti-chafing apparel. Using Google’s Shopping Graph of over 60 billion product listings, Search can show you tailored recommendations, side-by-side comparisons of in-stock options, and even local availability, helping you find the exact gear you need to race with confidence.

entries.title: The Gemini app is now available for Windows
entries.content:
Today, we're launching the Gemini app for Windows. Designed to work seamlessly alongside your favorite tools and daily applications, the new desktop app gives you instant assistance without breaking your flow.

Here are three ways you can use the Gemini app on your PC:

1. Access Gemini instantly with a keyboard shortcut.

Press Alt + Space on your PC at any time to open Gemini over your active work. Whether you need a quick fact-check on a document or a few catchy title ideas for a presentation, you can get the help you need and jump right back into your workflow.

2. Power through deep work in a dedicated workspace.

Inside the new app, you can access everything you use Gemini for already. Hand off multi-step tasks to Gemini Spark 1 , your 24/7 personal AI agent, or ask Gemini to draft a project summary by pulling information directly from your Google apps like Gmail and Google Drive.

3. Create images and videos.

Bring creative concepts to life directly from your desktop. You can generate custom images with Nano Banana for a presentation, direct a high-quality video with Gemini Omni 1 , and best of all you can do it all in one convenient place.

Lightweight and quiet, the app runs without slowing down your PC. This is just the beginning for the Gemini app on Windows, with more native desktop capabilities rolling out over time. The app is available today globally for Windows 10 and 11. Download the app at gemini.google/desktop.

entries.title: Switching password managers is easy and safe on Android
entries.summary: Android bot showing how to switch password managers
entries.content:
We believe you should have control over your digital life, including the freedom to choose the security tools that work best for you.

With that in mind, today we're introducing a new experience on Android to help you safely and easily move your passwords and passkeys between password managers in just a few clicks — no file downloads required. This gives you more flexibility, all while keeping your information safe.

Transfer passwords and passkeys with ease.

Historically, moving your passwords meant downloading them into an unencrypted text file, which left them unprotected on your device. And passkeys couldn't be transferred at all, so you'd have to recreate them across multiple sites and apps. Now, moving your passwords and passkeys to a new password manager is simpler and safer. Here’s what you can expect when making a switch 1 .

  • Start the move: Open your new password manager app and choose the option to import or copy your passwords and passkeys from another provider. The password manager will then hand the task over to Android.
  • Let Android securely coordinate the data transfer: Android will automatically detect existing password managers on your device and show you which you can import from.
  • Review and authorize: Once you tap “Continue,” Android will bring you to your existing password manager to select, review, and authorize the transfer. Then your data will be quickly and securely transferred between the apps in just a few seconds.

Import your passwords to Google Password Manager with just a few clicks. Exporting your data is just as easy.

Manage your data, your way.

This new transfer experience is already available on Google Password Manager, 1Password, Bitwarden Password Manager, and Dashlane, with more partners to follow. It is designed to give you always have complete control over your data and the freedom to switch providers whenever you want.

For a step-by-step walkthrough, read more about importing your passwords and passkeys in our Help Center.

entries.title: Drive profitable growth with new data and measurement tools
entries.content:
Earlier this year, we shared our vision for transforming measurement from a reactive report card to a proactive performance engine. That momentum requires three elements working in harmony:

  • A strong data foundation to fuel AI,
  • Multiple signals to see the full picture, and
  • Causal proof to drive real-world results.

Today, we’re announcing new capabilities across our measurement suite that can help you make better, faster decisions that drive business growth.

Unify your first-party signals to supercharge AI for your goals

To unlock AI’s full potential, you need a strong data foundation. We’ve spent years investing in tools like Google tag and Data Manager to simplify how you manage and activate your customer data. Today, we’re taking that commitment even further with three new enhancements to help you seamlessly unify your data across platforms and steer your AI toward profitable growth:

Break down data silos to boost AI-powered growth: We are directly integrating Data Manager into Google Analytics (GA) and Display & Video 360 (DV360), to help you manage and activate your first-party data across tools. Advertisers who connect offline and app data to Data Manager see an average 26% increase in incremental ROAS. 1 We’re also launching enhanced conversions in GA and DV360 to securely match customer data and improve ad relevance. Advertisers using enhanced conversions realize an average 11% increase in Search conversions compared to standard conversion imports. 2

Set up simple and secure data pipelines: To help you activate your data across more of the digital ecosystem, the Data Manager API is now universal. Based on the IAB Tech Lab’s Event and Conversions API (ECAPI) standard, the Data Manager API gives you a unified, secure setup to connect, manage, and activate your audiences and measurement across major ad platforms. And new built-in diagnostics in Data Manager can automatically identify and address data issues before they impact campaign performance.

Quantify short and long term value: Every new signal you share improves your performance today and builds even stronger results over time. That’s why we’re introducing a new Data Strength Uplift Metric in Google Ads. This metric calculates the additional conversions recovered by your first-party data setup to help quantify impact. Advertisers who build their data strength with Google tag gateway observe on average a 14% conversion uplift, 3 and over 20% uplift for their Demand Gen campaigns 4 .

Prove business impact with upgrades to Meridian

With a durable data foundation in place, the next step is evaluating what actually creates incremental demand. To help you connect those dots, we’re sharing our latest upgrades to Meridian — our open-source Marketing Mix Model (MMM) — making modeling faster, agentic, and directly calibrated with real-world causal proof:

Turn complex econometrics into actionable insights: We’re bringing new agentic capabilities into Meridian to help you audit data quality, resolve errors, and guide model building in real time. These new features are designed to help you deliver better outcomes for your business faster and across more ad platforms. What’s more, we’ve made significant updates to Meridian’s back end, so your analyses can run faster and more efficiently.

Prove the real business value of your brand investments: You can now include relevant brand signals (e.g. Branded Google Query Volume) directly in Meridian models, so you can measure the full effect of brand building, and show how upper-funnel video and TV campaigns lead to future sales.

Ground your measurement in real-world proof: Earlier this year, we introduced a new beta for Meridian GeoX, our global open-source library for running causal geo-experiments across any advertising platform. Now, GeoX is generally available globally in Meridian, so you can get started with running independent experiments, or incorporating incrementality results into your MMM to help boost accuracy.

Drive growth with your new measurement playbook

To learn how you can put this playbook into action — helping you strengthen your data foundation and prove the real financial return of every marketing dollar — secure your virtual front-row seat to Rethink 2026.

entries.title: Exploring Creative Intelligence with London’s Southbank Centre
entries.summary: Southbank Centre Creative Intelligence poster with logos and dates
entries.content:
This weekend, the Southbank Centre in London becomes a playground for creative technologies during the inaugural Creative Intelligence weekend, curated by PACT, Planetary Art Culture Technology.

Emerging computational tools are fundamentally reshaping how art is made and experienced. For a public art institution and Europe’s largest art centre celebrating its 75th anniversary, this shift poses important questions about how to work with artists to innovate with technology whilst celebrating human creative agency.

It is this inquiry that has informed the collaboration between Southbank Centre and Google Arts & Culture to date, from celebrating Hayward Gallery at 50 and digitising Art by Post to hosting four interactive experiments from the Arts & Culture Lab in the public foyers this weekend.

A Public Playground for the Imagination

In the Royal Festival Hall’s Clore Ballroom and Exploration Bazaar, visitors can experience Google Arts & Culture interactive experiments that harness AI

  • Dreaming with Flamingos by Yinka Ilori: Weaves West African folklore with Google DeepMind’s advanced AI music generation tool, Lyria, in an interactive riddle quest to restore a park's lost wisdom

Unlock Yinka Ilori’s musical playground

  • Splash Canvas by David Li: Gemini and fluid dynamics power squishy sea creatures who act as your paintbrushes and real-time art critics

Paint on a squishy, fluid canvas guided by AI sea creatures

  • Learn Everything: Uses Gemini to turn photos of everyday objects into visual metaphors for understanding complex topics.

Turn everyday objects into instant science lessons

  • Say What You See: A puzzle game that sharpens prompt literacy by reverse-engineering AI imagery.

Learn the art of prompting

Visionary voices across the weekend

The wider weekend brings together leading artists whose practices explore art and code — including several Google Arts & Culture has collaborated with over many years:

  • Alexandra Daisy Ginsberg: The artist presents her algorithmic garden work Pollinator Pathmaker on the Riverside Terrace. The work uses an algorithmic tool to design living gardens for pollinating insects rather than human taste, transforming art into a platform for non-human agency. Google Arts & Culture was an early supporter of the work.
  • Xin Liu: Ahead of her upcoming residency with Berlin's LAS Art Foundation and Google Arts & Culture, artist Xin Liu explores art, science, and ecology through a performance lecture.
  • Lex Fefegha: Google Arts & Culture Lab Artist in Residence, Lex brings Future Inventions to Southbank Centre with Peckham Digital for workshops exploring creative tech through an Afrocentric lens.

Experience the weekend from Friday 11 September to Sunday 13 September 2026 at the Southbank Centre, or explore the experiments online via Google Arts & Culture.
